description.narrative:
Sida bidrar med 34 000 000 SEK under en period av tre år 2020-2022 till Cambodia Climate Change Alliance III. Stödet kanaliseras genom UNDPs landkontor och är en samfinansiering med EU och UNDP för att bidra till en utveckling i Kambodja som är mera motståndskraftig mot klimatförändringar och minskade utsläpp av växthusgaser.
Programmet bidrar till upptrappning av arbetet för att motverka klimatförändringarna med fokus på samordning av institutioner (National Council for Sustainable Development, Ministry of Economy and Finance) och fem strategiska sektorministerier (Environment; Public Works and Transport; Rural Development; Mines and Energy; samt Education, Youth and Sports).
Den totala budgeten för insatsen är 11 868 895 USD. Det svenska stödet om 34 000 000 SEK, EU bidrar med 6 730 800 USD, UNDP med 500 000 USD och den kambodjanska staten med 336 900 USD in-kind (personal, lokaler, mm).

Sida contributes with 34 000,000 SEK during a period of three years 2020-2022 to carry out Cambodia Climate Change Alliance III. The support is channeled through UNDP country office, and is co-financed by EU and UNDP, and will contribute to a Cambodia development path that is increasingly climate-resilient and low carbon, measured by the level of green house gas emissions reduced.
The programme contributes towards a scale-up response to climate change, with a focus on coordinating institutions (National Council for Sustainable Development, Ministry of Economy and Finance) and five strategic sector ministries (Environment; Public Works and Transport; Rural Development; Mines and Energy; and Education, Youth and Sports).
The total budget for the intervention is 11 868 895 USD. The Swedish contribution is 34 000 000 SEK, EU contributes with 6 730 800 USD, UNDP with 500 000 USD, and the Cambodian Government with 336 900 USD in-kind (staff, facilities, etc.).

The programme aims to address the strategic challenges that Cambodia has faced to implement its climate change (CC) response at scale. In relation to the key challenges (immediate causes) the programme will act on three major drivers of change:
1. Improving capacity to produce, use, manage and disseminate locally relevant climate change information and research, addressing current knowledge gaps. For instance, the lack of reliable data on gender impacts of CC, and more generally on the distributional impacts of CC across various vulnerable groups, including the poor, landless, older people and children. This clearly also ties in with not only the importance of gender but also the right's perspective. The key assumption is that solid, locally-produced, policy relevant evidence will play a cruicial role in effective advocacy with decision-makers and help create political space for the institutional and systemic changes that are required to achieve Cambodia's climate objectives.
2. Integrating climate change in the policy, regulations, programmes and budgets of priority sectors. The main assumption is that effective mainstreaming of CC in ministries and sub-national systems and policies will be achieved through a combination of tailored advocacy (to create political space), adjustment to planning and budgeting procedures and related training, mentoring, policy advisory support, etc. A secondary assumption is that the changes can only happen during the programme period if there already is a demonstrated commitment of the concerned institutions' leadership. This assumption has guided the selection of ministerial partners.
3. Establishing a policy environment and financing tools to leverage private and public flows of development finance for the climate change response. An important link can be found here between this driver and the Cambodia UN Development Assistance Framework (UNDAF): by 2023 women and men in Cambodia, in particular those marginalised and vulnerable, live in a safe, healthy, secure and ecologically balanced environment with improved livelihoods, and are resilient to natural, socio-economic and CC related trends and shocks.

Cambodia Climate Change Alliance is in its third phase and is well established at an institutional level with the secretariat hosted by the National Council for Sustainable Development/Climate Change Department (NCSD/CCD). The alliance has been pioneer of for climate action in Least Development Countries (LDCs) and the level of national ownership is high. CCCA has as the flagship climate change programme in the country received support for the highest level of government. The NCSD/CCCA demonstrated strong leadership in coordinating the exercise to update Cambodia's Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC) to the Paris Agreement. The final NDC were technically more advanced and more detailed than the previous version and it includes several cross-cutting issues like gender equality and private sector engagement in a novel and well integrated manner. The document will be the basis for the country´s climate agenda in terms of both mitigation and adaptation and consultative approach to drafting the report will ensure stronger ownership and quality with key ministries and in key sectors. Waste management and agriculture are two sectors that were previously missing but that have now been included. CCCA has also been supporting NCSD to lead the process of developing Cambodia Long-Term Strategy for Carbon Neutrality that has still not be finalized and submitted to United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC).
The third phase of the Alliance builds on the results of previous phases and although only being implemented for 18 months there has been several significant achievements. For examples, the process of achieving the accreditation of a national institution to the Green Climate Fund (GCF) was long but eventually the National Committee for Sub-National Democratic Development was able to fulfil the stringent requirements of the GCF. Monitoring and reporting are important aspects for securing international climate finance and implementing the country´s NDC commitments. CCCA has both developed and digitized the national Green House Gass (GHG) inventory data which is managed by NCSD/CCD. CCCA has also developed an online system for inter-ministerial reporting on sectoral implementation of climate action. This will facilitate and enrich reporting to UNFCCC but also provide useful input to the coordinating the implementation to the country´s NDCs.
The Department of Climate Change has also been supported on the implementation of the third round the the Knowledge, Attitudes and Practices study, which provides key insights into how Cambodians understand and respond to climate change. For an independent perspective on the climate change response, CCCA also worked in partnership with the regional UNDP programme on the governance of climate finance (funded by Sida(reg asia)) to empower civil society organizations to review climate change expenditure and engage in dialogue with government and parliamentarians. This resulted in two climate change change citizen budgets, were Civil Society are invited to review and comment on public climate expenditures. CCCA has also overseen the annual Climate Public Expenditure Reviews in collaboration with the Ministry of Finance.
Some more specific examples of impact on beneficiaries were reported during these initial 18 months:
The water and hygiene intervention supported through TS1001 has provided resilient access to safe water to three communes, covering 8,053 households.This activity has benefited 13,176 ID poor households of 263 communes in 17 provinces.
The community forestry (CF) intervention has allowed for increasing the scale of the community forestry credit schemes in 10 locations, with a total capital increase from USD 35,430 to USD 49,364, and a proportional increase in revenues for forestry activities (patrolling, fire prevention activities etc.).
The project has benefited 960 households (4,914 individual beneficiaries) through both CF credit and reforestation activities (cash for work, benefiting 506 CF members 268 female or 53%) covering a total of 34.8 hectars (69,700 seedlings) in 4 locations.
Users of 10 health centers and one hospital in Tbong Khmum and Takeo provinces have benefited from continued electric supply (solar) for keeping vaccines and other medicine refrigerated.
CCCA supported a brief to the Deputy Prime Minister, Minister of Economy and Finance, on the implications of the Renewable Energy 100 initiative for investments in Cambodia
On vehicle taxation, CCCA supported a brief to the Ministry of Finance on potential changes to the import tax regime to promote more efficient vehicles.
In Ministry of Public Works and Transport, CCCA is supporting a policy/regulatory review of bottlenecks for the introduction of electric 2-wheelers in Cambodia.
CCCA has also awarded 7 small grants to projects that that are innovative and that can have significantly reduce the impact of the convid19 pandemic. These project are still ongoing.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
